answer: In the combined logistic regression (efficacy_bin ~ BMI + Age + Gender, n=80, PR=1 vs. PD/SD=0), the Wald p-value for Age as a predictor of treatment response is p = 0.0025 (coefficient −0.0795, SE 0.0263, z = −3.02; OR per year ≈ 0.924, 95% conclusion: older age is significantly associated with lower odds of PR). The model converged normally. Sensitivity check (PR vs. PD only, excluding SD): Age p = 0.0066 — the same direction and still significant, so the primary result is stable under the alternative reading. Only the primary result (p = 0.0025) goes in the final answer.
